expert intuition may use implicit configural processing that is not articulable and therefore cannot be accumulated.","The 'orthogonality' claim assumes cue coverage and integration capacity are independent dimensions; they may interact (e.g., more cues make integration harder)."],"overturn_conditions":["If the crowd-evolved checklist encodes interactions, the configural limitation is overturned and the panel may dominate unconditionally.","If panelists add spontaneous configural judgment, the panel may match experts on interaction items despite a flat checklist."],"shared_structure":["Both distinguish cue coverage (breadth of features) from configural integration (ability to represent interactions), and both predict that improving coverage does not fix integration capacity.","Both identify interaction-heavy items as the critical test case where coverage and integration diverge.","Both predict that a flat checklist, regardless of authorship, fails on configural items while a configural processor does not."],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_001","SCR_005","SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["The orthogonality claim transfers: improving authorship shifts the bias boundary but does not fix the configural limitation.","The diagnostic (structured errors on interaction-heavy items) transfers as unchanged evidence even under the crowd-evolved mechanism."]},"claim":"If the checklist is crowd-evolved via outcome feedback (Delphi with verifiable outcomes), the 'lossy compression' objection fails and the panel+checklist may exceed any single expert; but the distinguishing evidence remains the same: structured errors on interaction-heavy items, because crowd-evolution improves cue coverage but does not add configural integration capacity.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the crowd-evolved checklist includes interaction terms or decision-tree structure, it is not a flat checklist and the configural limitation does not apply.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If panelists spontaneously add configural judgment on top of the crowd-evolved checklist, the panel may match experts on interaction-heavy items.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If interaction-heavy items are absent from the evaluation, the configural failure mode is unobservable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the task class has no configural structure (purely additive), the crowd-evolved checklist dominates unconditionally.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A crowd-evolved checklist (iterated with outcome feedback) can accumulate cues from many experts and may encode a richer cue-set than any single expert's intuition. This invalidates the mechanism that the checklist is a lossy compression of one expert: the checklist is a superset. However, if the checklist remains a flat (additive) list, it cannot represent configural interactions. Panelists complying with a rich flat checklist will still fail on tasks requiring interaction effects. The distinguishing evidence is therefore unchanged: structured errors on interaction-heavy items reveal the limitation of even a crowd-evolved checklist, while success on such items would indicate genuine configural understanding (either via panelists adding judgment or via the checklist encoding interactions). The bias boundary is shifted (lower bias) but the configural failure mode is orthogonal to authorship.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
